# 0009: Specific status codes, require Content-Length, never 503

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-16
- **Modules:** upload-service, local
- **Source:** design doc, section "Status codes and Content-Length" (linked from README.md in this folder)

## Decision

Answer with specific codes and require Content-Length. Requiring a length lets the service stream with no buffering and
reject large files before reading them. Phones do not retry 429 and lose nothing: `app.log` carries its lines into the
next upload and the other files are full copies every time.

The codes: 400 for a bad name or a body that ends before Content-Length, 403 for a disabled type or an identity
problem, 408 for a body that stops arriving, 411 with no length, 413 when too large, 429 for the rate limit, a key
collision and storage failures. Tomcat sends the 400 and 408 for a broken body itself; the service records the same code
so the log line matches what the phone got.

## Rules for agents

Never return 503, and never read the body before every check has passed.

docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md-10-| MAC in the certificate | Subject CN, 12 hex digits, uppercase, no separators. No SAN. File names carry the MAC in lowercase. | Read the MAC from the CN and compare case-insensitively (ADR 0004). |
docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md-11-| TLS | TLS 1.2 only on all three phones. Shared ciphers: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384. | The ALB policy must allow these on TLS 1.2 (ADR 0003). |
docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md-12-| Certificate chain | Phones send 3 certificates (leaf and 2 intermediates); with the root the chain is 4. Device certificates are valid for 15 years. | Exactly at the ALB depth limit of 4, so it must be tested on a real ALB. Phones made before about late 2011 may carry expired certificates; how the ALB treats them is open. |
docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md:13:| Reaction to status codes | Retry only on 503: 3 tries, 1 s apart, identical body. Retry-After ignored. 405, 429, 413, 411, 400 and 403 get one try. A 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves app.log stuck for 300 s and holds back the phone's other uploads. | Always reject before 100 Continue. Never 503; prefer 429 when overloaded (ADR 0009). Keys must cope with identical calls.xml copies within 2 s (ADR 0011). |
docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md-14-| File names | `<mac>-app.log`, `<mac>-boot.log` (VVX only), `<mac>-calls.xml`. Manual upload: `<mac>-now-app.log`, `<mac>-now-boot.log`; `-now-` comes right after the MAC. | Accept `-now-` after the MAC. Don't require boot.log; the Edge never sends it (ADR 0007). |
docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md-15-| What each upload holds | app.log holds only the lines added since the last successful upload, plus any failed lines. `-now-` files and calls.xml are full copies every time. | Store the pieces; joining them in order rebuilds the log. Expect one full app.log per phone at migration. Nothing is lost on a 429. |
docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md-16-| Backlog after an outage | After a 15-minute outage the phone sends nothing until something new happens. No log lines or call-list changes were lost. A 1-5-9 call made during the outage was dropped. | No upload flood when the service comes back. |
--

3. The ALB headers identify the caller (403).
    4. The certificate MAC equals the file name MAC, in any case (403).
    5. Content-Length is present (411).
    6. Content-Length is within the type's limit (413).

    Only then does the service read the body, streaming it to S3 with a create-only write. It
    answers 200 once S3 has the whole file, and 429 if S3 refuses or fails the write.

    The service never answers 503. No response has a body.
paths:
  /logs/{file}:
    parameters:
      - name: file
        in: path
        required: true
        description: |
          `<mac>-<type>`, or `<mac>-now-<type>` for an upload the user started. The MAC is
          12 hex digits in any case with no separators. Accepted types: app.log, boot.log
          (both also with now-) and calls.xml. Any other name, or a path with more or fewer
          segments, gets 400.
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}-((now-)?(app|boot)\.log|calls\.xml)$'
        examples:
          appLog:
            value: 0004f2abcdef-app.log
          manualBootLog:
            value: 0004f2abcdef-now-boot.log
    put:
      summary: Upload one log file
      operationId: uploadLog
      parameters:
        - name: Content-Length
          in: header
          required: true
          description: The body size in bytes. A chunked upload has none and gets 411.
          schema:
            type: integer
            format: int64
            minimum: 0
          example: 48213
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertSubject'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertIssuer'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertValidity'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertSerialNumber'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertLeaf'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ForwardedFor'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        description: The file, sent as it is. The service does not read it until every check passes.
        content:
          '*/*':
            schema:
              type: string
              format: binary
      responses:
        '200':
          description: |
            S3 has the whole file, stored under a key made from the MAC, the server's UTC receive
            time to the millisecond, and the type.
        '400':
          description: |
            One of:

            - BAD_FILE_NAME: the path after /logs/ is not an accepted file name, for example
              `0004f2abcdef-phone.cfg`, `0004f2abcd-app.log` or `extra/0004f2abcdef-app.log`.
            - BODY_INCOMPLETE: the connection ended before Content-Length bytes arrived. Tomcat
              answers this itself when its read of the body fails, and the service records the
              same code.
        '403':
          description: |
            One of:

            - FILE_TYPE_DISABLED: the type is turned off in `device-logs.file-types`. calls.xml
              is off by default until the privacy review (ADR 0008).
            - UNTRUSTED_IDENTITY: the ALB headers do not identify the caller. A certificate
              header is missing or repeated, the leaf does not parse, its CN is not 12 uppercase
              hex digits or differs from the Subject header, or X-Forwarded-For has no last entry.
            - MAC_MISMATCH: the certificate CN is a different MAC from the file name, for
              example certificate `0004F2ABCDEF` uploading `0004f2000000-app.log`.
        '408':
          description: |
            BODY_TIMEOUT. The body stopped arriving for longer than Tomcat's connection timeout.
            Tomcat answers this itself, and the service records the same code.
        '411':
          description: LENGTH_REQUIRED. The request has no Content-Length, for example because it is chunked.
        '413':
          description: |
            TOO_LARGE. Content-Length is above the type's `max-size` in `device-logs.file-types`,
            10 MB by default.
        '429':
          description: |
            The file may not have been stored. Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost:
            app.log carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are full copies
            every time. One of:

            - KEY_EXISTS: another file of this type from this phone was stored in the same
              millisecond. Nothing is overwritten, and the next upload gets a new receive time
              (ADR 0011).
            - STORAGE_FAILED: S3 failed the write or it ran past its 60 s deadline. Once the whole
              body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the deadline. Never 503.
    head:
      summary: Always 404
      description: Each upload stands alone, so there is never a stored file to compare against.
      operationId: headLog

content.text:
**Why never 503:** In the lab, phones retry only on 503. They try 3 times, 1 s apart, with the identical body, and ignore Retry-After. A 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves `app.log` stuck for 300 s and holds back the phone's other uploads. A storage failure happens after the body has started streaming, so a 503 there would trigger exactly that. ADR 0009 therefore says never 503 and use 429 for the rate limit, key collisions and storage failures.

**Why 429 loses nothing:** Phones get one try on 429 and don't retry, so the failed upload is simply dropped. No data is lost because of what each upload contains:
- `app.log` holds only the lines added since the last successful upload, plus any lines that failed. Lines from a 429'd upload go out again with the next one.
- `-now-` files and `calls.xml` are full copies every time, so the next upload replaces the missed one.

The lab also found that after a 15-minute outage no log lines were lost. One more detail from `openapi.yaml`: if S3 ran past its 60 s deadline after the whole body was sent, it may still commit the object, so a 429 doesn't always mean the file wasn't stored.

Files used:
- `docs/architecture/decisions/0009-status-codes-and-content-length.md`
- `docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md` (rows "Reaction to status codes", "What each upload holds" and "Backlog after an outage")
- `upload-service/openapi.yaml` (the 429 / STORAGE_FAILED description)
- `upload-service/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/web/RejectionStatusMapper.java`
- `upload-service/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/policy/Rejection.java`
